title: Review: Apple's M6 MacBook Pro is good, but it's missing all the exciting stuff
gist: Apple's entry-level M6 14-inch MacBook Pro brings a strong M6 chip (12 CPU cores, 12 GPU cores, 32-core Neural Engine) but keeps the 2021 design without the new OLED touchscreen, while its starting price rose to $1,999 with mandatory 1TB storage amid RAM and storage shortages. The reviewer calls it good but awkwardly positioned versus the MacBook Air.

insights.claim: Apple's entry-level 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro starts at $1,999, $400 more than the M5 model's launch price and $700 more than the 2020 M1 MacBook Pro, partly due to a mandatory 1TB storage upgrade and a June price increase.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple is passing memory/storage cost inflation to consumers via mix-up — supportive of ASPs but a risk to Mac unit volumes.
insights.locator: In other words, it has very little of what makes

insights.claim: Apple raised most of its prices in June and the reviewer attributes abnormal technology progression to ongoing RAM and storage shortages.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Memory shortages are pushing through to consumer device pricing — a tailwind for DRAM/NAND suppliers and a headwind for PC demand.
insights.quote: the times are still anything but normal, mostly thanks to the ongoing RAM and storage shortages.
insights.locator: After all, the OLED MacBook Pros haven't even fully replaced

insights.claim: The base M6 MacBook Pro lacks the touchscreen, OLED panel, Dynamic Island, weight reduction and glowing logo of Apple's new high-end 'PROLED XDR' MacBook Pros, which start at $2,899.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple's OLED touchscreen MacBook upgrade cycle is concentrated at the high end for now.
insights.locator: This year's entry-level MacBook Pro mostly falls into that latter category.

insights.claim: It is hard to justify the base MacBook Pro's $500 to $700 premium over the 13- or 15-inch MacBook Air now that it no longer has Apple's best screen, especially for buyers who don't need 1TB of storage.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Expect demand to skew toward the Air or the OLED Pro, hollowing out the middle tier.
insights.locator: The long and short of it is that this isn't a bad laptop

insights.claim: Apple's M6 has 12 CPU cores (two super cores, four performance, six efficiency), 12 GPU cores and a doubled 32-core Neural Engine, while RAM options remain 16/24/32GB with memory bandwidth of 153GB/s (16GB) or 170GB/s (24/32GB).
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Doubling NPU cores signals Apple's on-device AI push, but RAM caps remain the binding constraint for local models.
insights.locator: The M6 gets more CPU cores

insights.claim: The 16GB M6 MacBook Pro delivers about 7 percent better single-core, 15 percent better multi-core CPU and 20-30 percent better GPU performance than the M5 MacBook Pro, and 30-60 percent gains over the M3 model.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Meaningful upgrade for M1/M2-era users supports a Mac replacement cycle, but M4/M5 owners have little reason to upgrade.
insights.locator: The chip is still a solid upgrade from the M5.

insights.claim: Under load the M6 is faster than the M5 while drawing the same power, making it more power-efficient.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Continued perf-per-watt gains sustain Apple Silicon's laptop efficiency advantage over x86 rivals.
insights.locator: Finally, a word on power usage.

insights.claim: Because the M6 has shipped only in base Macs while Pro/Max models remain on M5, the cheaper M6 machines deliver Apple's best single-core CPU performance and the larger Neural Engine; rumors suggest the M6 will get no Pro, Max or Ultra variants.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple's chip cadence is fragmenting across tiers, which may reflect supply or cost constraints on high-end silicon.
insights.locator: As with the Mac mini, the basic MacBook Pro getting an M6

insights.claim: The reviewer predicts at least a two-year wait before OLED touchscreens trickle down to the base MacBook Pro, first replacing non-OLED M5 Pro/Max models, mirroring how OLED and ProMotion moved from iPhone Pro to standard iPhones.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Laptop OLED panel demand from Apple should broaden over 2027-2028, relevant to OLED panel suppliers.
insights.quote: I would not be surprised if we were left waiting at least two years for an OLED touchscreen to trickle down to this laptop.
insights.locator: That's to be expected, I suppose

insights.claim: The base MacBook Pro remains the cheapest Apple laptop with a 120Hz ProMotion mini-LED display and the $150 nano-texture anti-glare option, plus more ports than the MacBook Air and active cooling for sustained workloads.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Display and thermals remain the base Pro's only differentiators as the Air will likely get M6 too.
